holidays.name: National Siblings Day
holidays.description: A day for celebrating your brothers and sisters, whether you adore them, argue with them, or still hold a grudge over a stolen toy from 1994. Folks post throwback photos, send goofy texts, and fondly recall childhood mischief.
holidays.origin: Founded by Claudia Evart, who started the observance in 1995 in memory of siblings she lost. She chose April 10 for her late brother and sister, and she has worked for years to get it recognized across the U.S.
holidays.funFact: Claudia Evart lost both a brother and a sister, and she created the day to honor all sibling bonds. It has been recognized by many U.S. governors and is widely celebrated on social media.

holidays.name: National Encourage a Young Writer Day
holidays.description: A day to nurture the next generation of storytellers by cheering on any kid or teen who loves to scribble stories, poems, or fan fiction. Praise a first draft, hand over a notebook, or resist the urge to correct their spelling.
holidays.origin: An informal, grassroots observance that grew out of literacy and creative-writing communities. It is meant to remind adults that encouragement can matter more than red-pen edits.
holidays.funFact: Many famous authors began writing as children. Jane Austen wrote hilarious parody stories as a teen, which she later gathered into notebooks known as her Juvenilia.

holidays.name: National Hug Your Dog Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to squeezing your canine companion and giving them the cuddles they deserve, whether or not they enjoy being hugged. Dogs everywhere either wag with joy or give you the side-eye of tolerance.
holidays.origin: A pet-lover observance that circulates through pet-themed calendars and social media. It is not official, but it spreads each year thanks to dog owners who need no excuse to cuddle their pups.
holidays.funFact: Many dog behaviorists note that some dogs find hugs stressful, since dogs do not hug each other. Many dogs show their feelings through leaning, tail wags, and belly rubs instead.

holidays.name: National Cinnamon Crescent Day
holidays.description: A sweet celebration of flaky, buttery, cinnamon-swirled crescent pastries. It is the perfect excuse to eat a pastry for breakfast, lunch, and dessert.
holidays.origin: A food-calendar observance that, like many pastry holidays, comes from bakery and food-lover traditions. Its exact origin is unclear, but fans of cinnamon treats gladly keep it alive.
holidays.funFact: The crescent shape of pastries is often linked to the croissant, which is a French descendant of the Austrian kipferl. A popular legend ties the crescent shape to a 1683 siege of Vienna, though historians doubt the tale.

holidays.name: National Farm Animals Day (Unofficial Barnyard Celebration)
holidays.description: A day to appreciate the cows, pigs, chickens, goats, and other barnyard characters who bring us milk, eggs, and endless entertainment. Visit a petting zoo or just practice your best moo.
holidays.origin: A loosely observed animal-appreciation day tied to farming and agricultural traditions, which tend to cluster in spring as baby animals arrive on farms.
holidays.funFact: Goats are famous for their curiosity and sometimes seem to have a sense of fun. Fainting goats stiffen when startled because of a genetic condition called myotonia congenita.
